name: resolve-issue
description: Turn a GitHub issue into a validated, ready-to-open pull request. A multi-agent workflow checks the issue is worth taking (closed, claimed, competing PRs, the repo's AI policy), reproduces the bug, fixes it, has an independent checker re-prove the fix, reviews it and drafts the PR. Four modes from a 2-agent triage to a thorough run, with effort levels and a hard agent cap. Nothing is pushed, posted or opened until you approve.

default_mode.title: Default mode
default_mode.description: How much work a run does when you don't name a mode: triage (is the issue worth taking?), quick, standard or thorough.

default_effort.title: Default effort
default_effort.description: How hard each agent thinks: low, medium, high or max, or inherit to use your session's effort level.

confirm_before_run.title: Ask before running
confirm_before_run.description: Show the run's size and ask once before it starts. Triage runs never ask.

publish_guard.title: Publish guard
publish_guard.description: Block git push and GitHub writes by subagents for 12 hours after a resolve-issue run starts in the session, and in resolve-issue worktrees until you approve a publish. A subagent's publishing command from a directory the guard cannot resolve, or a subagent's command past the guard's reading bounds, is blocked in any session. It reads command text: defense in depth, not a sandbox (see docs/safety.md).

autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.description: How much the skill decides about review findings on its own, only at validation gates, which cannot publish. ask: you decide every finding. minor: it settles low-impact, declined and informational findings, and asks before any fix. full: it also makes the fixes it recommends, up to the round limit. Publishing always waits for your approval.
